Use `test/qa/impersonate_target_contains_condition_snapshot_test.py`, class `TestImpersonateTargetContainsConditionSnapshotQA`, method `test_impersonate_target_contains_condition_snapshot_case`. The test does `result = OTHER_TARGET in SELF_TARGET`, which Python compiles into the call `SELF_TARGET.__contains__(OTHER_TARGET)`. `ImpersonateTarget.__contains__` is defined in `yt_dlp/networking/impersonate.py` at line 40. After the `isinstance` check at line 41 passes, control reaches the multi-conjunction return expression STARTING at line 43:
```
return (
    (self.client is None or target.client is None or self.client == target.client)
    and (self.version is None or target.version is None or self.version == target.version)
    and (self.os is None or target.os is None or self.os == target.os)
    and (self.os_version is None or target.os_version is None or self.os_version == target.os_version)
)
```
At the line-43 trace event (the moment Python evaluates this return condition), report the EXACT values of every attribute referenced by the condition. `SELF_TARGET` and `OTHER_TARGET` are the two `ImpersonateTarget` dataclass instances built at the top of the test file with literal kwargs. Inside `__contains__`, `self` is the LEFT operand of `in` (i.e. `SELF_TARGET`, the container) and `target` is the RIGHT operand (i.e. `OTHER_TARGET`, the value being checked). Return a JSON object with exactly these eight keys (each value is either a string or null): `self_client`, `target_client`, `self_version`, `target_version`, `self_os`, `target_os`, `self_os_version`, `target_os_version`.

62:    """
63:    Base class for request handlers that support browser impersonation.

74:                Set to None to disable this check.
75:                Note: Entries are in order of preference

79:                        Set to None to disable impersonation.
